requirements: Build an online marketplace handling 50k orders/day with flash-sale bursts of 10x traffic. Orders must survive payment-provider outages, customers see near-real-time order status, and the team (12 engineers) ships multiple times per day. PCI-DSS compliance applies.

E-commerce platform with catalog, cart, checkout and reviews. Team of 6, moderate traffic (500 req/s peak), wants independent deployment per team but struggles with Kafka operations. Strong consistency required for checkout payments.
Admin dashboard for marketplace sellers with complex forms and reports. 200 internal users, no public traffic, data volume under 100 GB. Budget is minimal and the team knows only Python/Django.

Payment processing platform: every state change must be auditable and replayable, disputes require full history reconstruction, and balance calculations must be exact. Throughput is 2k transactions/s.

Cross-border money transfer flow spanning compliance checks, FX quoting, debit, credit and notification steps. Each step is an independent service; a failed step must roll back completed steps via compensation. Steps take seconds to hours.
Read-heavy analytics API serving pre-aggregated trading dashboards; writes arrive as batches every 15 minutes, queries must answer in under 100 ms over billions of rows.
Fraud detection scoring for card transactions: decision required within 80 ms p99, model features need sub-millisecond reads, and rule changes deploy without redeploying the scoring path.

Hospital integration engine connecting HL7 devices, lab systems and billing. Protocols are heterogeneous and message transformation rules change per hospital. Cannot expose patient data outside the hospital network.
Patient-facing appointment booking app plus clinician portal with very different data shapes. Backends are shared services; each client team wants independent release cadence.
Ingest 100k IoT sensor readings per second, detect anomalies within 2 seconds, and keep only 7 days of raw data. Devices are flaky and reconnect often; cloud budget must stay flat as sensors grow.
Factory telemetry: nightly regulatory reports need exact full-history recomputation while operators also need second-level alerting on the live stream. One immutable log feeds both.
Offshore wind farm with 500 turbines and only intermittent satellite connectivity. Local decisions (blade pitch) must work fully offline; cloud aggregates daily for fleet analytics.

Nightly ETL: extract from 15 heterogeneous sources, cleanse, deduplicate and load into a warehouse. Volumes are 50 GB/night, ordering matters, and each cleansing step must be independently testable and restartable.
Company-wide data platform where each domain (sales, logistics, finance) publishes its own governed datasets; central team only provides discovery, contracts and storage tooling.

Document intelligence service: OCR ingestion, chunking, embedding, vector search and LLM answering. Multiple specialist models (layout, table, NER) incrementally refine a shared document representation; control logic decides which model runs next based on confidence.
Recommendation platform with weekly batch training and real-time feature serving; models are versioned, experiments must be reproducible, and drift triggers automatic retraining.
Multi-agent research assistant: planner agent decomposes questions, worker agents search and summarize, a supervisor retries failed agents. Agents never share memory directly, only messages.
Company marketing site plus blog with CMS editing. Traffic is 5 req/s, content changes daily, hosting budget is near zero, and the team is two developers.

B2B SaaS product at 3000 tenants with distinct module boundaries (billing, CRM, reporting). Single deployable is desired for ops simplicity, but modules must not reach into each other's tables and one module will be extracted to a service next year.
Public API product where third parties authenticate, discover rate limits and integrate; all traffic funnels through one managed entry point with per-tenant quotas and WAF.

A 15-year-old .NET monolith runs the business. We will move one capability (notifications) per quarter to new services, keeping the monolith running until each replacement is proven; traffic must switch gradually per endpoint.

Core insurance policy administration: pure business-rule domain (premiums, coverage, claims) that must be testable without any framework, with web, batch and partner-channel adapters around it. Rules change monthly.

Call-center desktop app for 5000 agents: rich UI panels that update independently, backed by domain services; agents navigate nested views (customer, ticket, knowledge base) that each manage their own state.
Backoffice tax-calculation service: forms-heavy UI, straightforward CRUD against a well-understood schema, 50 concurrent users, no elasticity needs.
Monte-Carlo risk simulation: master splits 10 million parameter combinations across 200 worker processes and aggregates results; workers are stateless and fail independently.

Warehouse robot fleet: a planner decomposes pick missions into tasks, executor robots run tasks and report status, and the planner reschedules on failure. Strict separation between deciding and doing.
Multiplayer game backend with 100k concurrent players in bursty sessions; player state lives in memory for millisecond reads and replicates asynchronously to persistent storage.
Real-time auction bidding service: accept 20k bids/s, never block on I/O in the hot path, apply backpressure when downstream persistence lags, and isolate bidder-partition failures.

Insurance claims adjudication: underwriters update eligibility and payout rules declaratively; rules fire against claim facts and every decision must be explainable. IT must not redeploy code to change a rule.

Photo pipeline: upload, virus scan, thumbnail, EXIF strip, face-tag and archive run in sequence; each stage scales independently and must be swappable without touching the others. Stages are stateless.
Holiday-photo sharing startup MVP: 3 developers, no ops team, unpredictable traffic, and a hard requirement to pay only for actual usage. Standard web + API workload.

Emerging-standard blockchain settlement network between banks: no central trust, smart contracts encode netting rules, and regulators require an appendable audit trail. Throughput is low (tens of transactions/s).
Self-diagnosing print fleet: firmware behavior must be adjusted at runtime based on observed error patterns; a meta layer inspects and patches the base control software while it runs.
Trading exchange matching engine: order intake is asynchronous and bursty, matching runs deterministically on a single thread for 2 million msgs/s, and persistence completes asynchronously.

IDE plugin platform: a small stable editor core with hundreds of third-party extensions loaded at runtime; extension crashes must not take down the editor and each extension declares its extension points.
Enterprise HR suite: 40 screen-flows over a stable data model with form validation and reporting. Classic request/response web app, one framework, one database, 4-developer team.
Regional bank moving core workloads to cloud over 3 years while keeping regulated ledger systems on-prem. One identity plane and one deployment pipeline must span both environments.
SaaS with EU data-residency and US low-latency requirements: identical workloads deployed to two providers, steered by latency and residency, with one CI/CD and one observability plane.
We need a system that ingests partner product feeds, normalizes them, and exposes a search API plus nightly exports. Team of 5, 2 M products, restock events arrive throughout the day.
Notification hub for a logistics company: delivery events from scanners, route updates from dispatch, and customer alerts across email/SMS/push. Peak 5k events/s, duplicates must not double-notify.
